The ledger maps 3.1 to dominance Q05 and simultaneous-tie Q30. Neither asks or states the ordinary immediate 30-VP win timing. This is a distinct terminal timing rule, not another tie example.
Q03 starts at ambush and Q59 only excludes coalition partners as enemies. Neither tests the attacking-presence and same-clearing prerequisites; this determines whether a battle can start at all.

Q03 names the before/after steps and removal priority but omits the effect-order decision makers. Q22 gives only the generic fallback. This is an explicit priority exception with consequential decision rights.

Q03 covers extra hits and defenselessness but not ignored-hit subtraction. Q49 instead covers the separate Vagabond rule for ignoring excess hits after no undamaged items remain. This is a named source branch, not different dice arithmetic.

The new element is the ordinary crafted item's source/destination. Q04 only checks absent-supply legality and card disposition, Q53 assumes a Crafted Items box without teaching how items enter it, and Q56 teaches only the Vagabond destination. Printed VP and card disposal are context already partly covered, not separately claimed novel.

Q04 speaks generically of crafting pieces, Q12 says craft first without naming roosts, and Q43 only rules out supporters. The bank does not identify Eyrie/Alliance crafting pieces or explain the wildcard crafting icon. These are source-defined cost/eligibility rules, not another arrangement of existing crafting pieces.

The ledger labels 8.5.1-3 Craft/mobilize/train but Q16 only teaches Train and Q43 only supporter restrictions. Mobilize is a missing full action; free interleaving is a faction timing distinction from Marquise/Eyrie craft-first turns.

Q13 states that scoring and draw/discard occur after Turmoil but never gives the rightmost-empty-space scoring procedure or draw formula. The rightmost-track scoring engine is a missing distinct faction rule; the draw text completes the phase without treating another numeric draw variant as novel.

The ledger maps 9.5.1-2 to Q17/Q49/Q61, but those questions cover movement and battle strength, not the sword-exhaustion Battle action cost. This is the missing action-cost rule, with readiness versus passive strength as the discriminating outcome.
Basic turn handoff is not the phase-boundary effects rule of Q23 or setup turn-order assignment of Q66.
Damage destination and unchanged exhaustion state are distinct from rolled-hit caps, repair/rest, track routing or permanently removing excess items.

Q47 asks available operation names, officer consumption and draw timing, not individual procedures. Fresh adjudication confirms the one-warrior-at-one-chosen-base Recruit rule is not explicitly tested elsewhere. This question directly tests that new core procedure plus the operation-budget rule.
Tests the currently unrequested 9.5 any-order-and-number phase permission. Item eligibility and Ranger are context already tested elsewhere, not counted as additional novelty.
